title: Semantic Component Analysis: Introducing Multi-Topic Distributions to Clustering-Based Topic Modeling
subcategory: clustering-based topic model with iterative linear decomposition (multi-topic per document)
task: Scalable multi-topic modelling of large, noisy short-text collections
problem: BERTopic assigns one topic per document and leaves many documents as noise; LLM-based topic models are too expensive for large data.
architecture: SCA: embed texts, reduce with UMAP (cosine, 5 dimensions) and cluster with HDBSCAN as in BERTopic; then a decomposition step turns cluster centroids into unit vectors (semantic components), removes them from the embeddings and repeats on the residuals; components with high token overlap are merged; each document can load on several components.
llm_or_encoder: Sentence embedding model (any); TopicGPT baselines with GPT-3.5 (copied) and Llama-3.2 1B/8B

datasets.name: Trump
datasets.details: all tweets by Donald Trump until December 2024 (60K samples)

datasets.name: Chinese News
datasets.details: 1.5M Chinese tweets from news outlets, collected and released by the authors

key_results: Topics found: 182 vs 55 (Trump), 331 vs 102 (Hausa), 594 vs 212 (Chinese News) for BERTopic, with noise rate close to 0 vs 0.275, 0.574 and 0.429.
Bills: P1 0.42, ARI 0.18, NMI 0.38; TopicGPT with Llama-3.2-8B gets 0.16, 0.00, 0.09, while the GPT-3.5 numbers copied from TopicGPT are 0.57, 0.42, 0.52.
strengths: Multiple topics per document with almost no unassigned documents.
Scales to 1.5M short texts and works in English, Hausa and Chinese.
Outperforms TopicGPT at a similar compute budget.

limitations.text: Modular pipeline can propagate errors (e.g. poor clusters lead to poor topics).
Topic quality depends on the embedding model, a problem for low-resource languages and domains.
Linear decomposition cannot capture non-linear multi-dimensional components.
Generic, over-predicted clusters and interpretability of topic representations remain to be addressed.
Topic diversity is lower than BERTopic (e.g. 0.703 vs 0.947 on Trump).
